description: Build all 15 new blog components in src/components/blog/ and rewrite blog.$slug.tsx to the rich two-column layout. Also update blog.index.tsx to show feature image thumbnails. Depends on FEAT-001 (the expanded data model must exist first).

2. Use a small pill with rounded-full bg-accent border border-border. - H1: heading-1 utility, mt-3. - Subtitle: if present, text-lg text-muted-foreground mt-2. - Author row: flex items-center gap-3 mt-4. Avatar: 40px circle or a fallback initials div. Name in font-semibold text-sm; brand line in text-xs text-muted-foreground. - Meta row (dates + read time): text-xs text-muted-foreground mt-1. Format dates with date-fns format(parseISO(date), 'MMMM d, yyyy'). Show 'Published {date}' and if updatedDate differs, 'Updated {updatedDate}'. Separator bullet ·. ReadTime. - No border or background — just clean text hierarchy.

with id={section.id}. H2 heading-2 mt-10 mb-4. Then render each ContentBlock by type: - paragraph:

7. Create src/components/blog/NewsletterSubscribe.tsx (globally reusable — no article-specific logic)
   Props: { heading?: string; subtext?: string; consentText?: string }
   State machine: type SubscribeState = 'idle' | 'loading' | 'success' | 'error'. Default heading='Stay Informed'. Default subtext='Get trusted wellness education delivered to your inbox.'. Consent text defaults to 'No spam. Unsubscribe any time. See Privacy Policy.'
   Implementation:
   - Form with react-hook-form + zod (z.object({ email: z.string().email() })). Import useForm from 'react-hook-form', zodResolver from '@hookform/resolvers/zod'.
   - onSubmit: set state to 'loading', simulate API call with setTimeout(1500) then set 'success'. On catch, set 'error'.
   - Email input: <Input type='email' ...> with aria-label and error message slot.
   - Submit button: bg-primary text-white, shows 'Subscribe' in idle, spinner + 'Subscribing…' in loading, disabled in loading/success states.
   - Success state: replace form with a green confirmation message 'You\'re on the list!' + subtext.
   - Error state: show red error message below the button.
   - Card wrapper: rounded-xl border border-border bg-card p-5.

8. Create src/components/blog/U20XPromo.tsx (globally reusable) Props: { headline?: string; copy?: string; ctaLabel?: string; ctaPath?: string; imageUrl?: string } Defaults: headline='TURN KNOWLEDGE INTO ACTION.', copy='The U20X™ 20-day challenge turns what you learn into a daily practice — real habits, real results.', ctaLabel='Take the Leap →', ctaPath='/u20x'. Implementation: - Outer wrapper: rounded-xl overflow-hidden. Background: style={{ background: 'linear-gradient(135deg, var(--u20x-navy) 0%, var(--u20x-blue) 100%)' }} text-white p-5. - Optional image at top if imageUrl provided: rounded-lg mb-4. - Headline: text-sm font-bold tracking-widest uppercase text-white/90 mb-1. - Copy: text-sm text-white/80 leading-relaxed mb-4. - CTA: with inline styles: bg-white text-u20x-navy font-semibold text-sm px-4 py-2 rounded-lg hover:bg-white/90. Use style={{ color: 'var(--u20x-navy)' }}. - Trust badges row: flex gap-3 mt-4. Three items: '✓ Real People', '✓ Real Habits', '✓ Real Results'. text-xs text-white/80.

findings: All 15 components built successfully in src/components/blog/. Build exits 0 with no TypeScript errors. Key implementation notes: (1) getProducts() from catalog.ts returns Product[] from the merged products array; used directly in RecommendedProducts.tsx. (2) Product media[].src may be a string or an imported image object — RecommendedProducts casts to string safely. (3) U20XPromo uses inline style for gradient since Tailwind v4 utility classes for arbitrary CSS variables aren't registered. (4) blog.index.tsx cards now wrap image above the padded content area (overflow-hidden + two-div pattern). (5) Mobile sidebar is rendered as a separate lg:hidden block after the article, in order: U20XPromo → NewsletterSubscribe → RecentArticles → TopicExplorer. (6) bun binary was not in the agent's PATH; build was verified via node_modules/.bin/vite build directly — exit code 0, no errors.
